PC: The first step should be stabilization of the patient, followed by surgical consultation.

| CBC + differential | Highly likely to be abnormal given time course and fevers; results may support clinical diagnosis | Provides a snapshot of lab abnormalities (e.g., leukocytosis, anemia); trend over time may be helpful | Labs should **not** be a reason to delay surgical consultation | Intermediate; higher value than in simple SSTI but lower value than immediate surgical consultation |

| CRP | Highly likely to be abnormal given time course and fevers; results may support clinical diagnosis | Trend over time may be most helpful | Labs should **not** be a reason to delay surgical consultation | Intermediate; higher value than in simple SSTI but lower value than immediate surgical consultation |

| Blood culture | Higher pre-test probability of being abnormal in ill-appearing patient | Could guide anti-microbial management | Labs should **not** be a reason to delay surgical consultation | Intermediate; higher value than in simple SSTI but lower value than immediate surgical consultation |

| Ultrasound | Helpful if thrombosis or thrombophlebitis is suspected; however, this does not fit as well with patient's history and presentation | Depends on quality and experience of ultrasonographer | When necrotizing infection is suspected, ultrasound will delay appropriate care | Low |

| MRI | Indicated for this patient who has failed appropriate empiric therapy, now with systemic toxicity and clinical worsening | Provides most detailed view of skin and soft tissue planes | MRI should **not** be a reason to delay surgical consultation | Intermediate |
| Empiric Antibiotics | N/A |  |  | High. Adjunctive therapy; *not* *curative* without surgical intervention |
MK: When a patient presents with systemic toxicity (e.g., fevers, malaise, nausea, vomiting, SIRS/sepsis) in the setting of worsening SSTI, and/or atypical exam features are present (e.g., pain out of proportion; spreading edema and erythema), you should have a high index of suspicion for necrotizing SSTI.
SBP: | ID consult | Consultation not necessary to start empiric therapy for necrotizing infection | ID may be able to assist with local resistance patterns (e.g., for MRSA) | ID consultation should not be a reason to delay care or to start empiric antibiotics | Low |

| General Surgery consult | When necrotizing infection is suspected, this is first-line. STAT page. | Surgical exploration and debridement are both diagnostic and therapeutic; an experienced surgeon's exam can be extremely valuable | If false positive – risk of anesthesia and surgery | **Highest value – both for diagnosis and treatment** |
